candidates.title: Religious health-care facilities can continue to ban MAID on site, B.C. Supreme Court rules
candidates.description: The B.C. Supreme Court has upheld the exemption that allows religious health-care facilities to prohibit medical assistance in dying. The decision means facilities such as Vancouver’s St. Paul’s Hospital can continue to require patients that want MAID to transfer to another facility.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Interpol joins search for missing Edmonton children as father faces kidnapping charges
candidates.description: Edmonton police say they are working with international agencies to locate an Edmonton man, who is facing kidnapping charges, and his two children.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pedestrian killed in crash involving off-duty Vancouver police officer
candidates.description: A woman was killed in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood Friday morning in a crash involving an off-duty police officer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa flyer business apologizes for its part in spreading 'known romance scam'
candidates.description: An eastern Ontario flyer business is apologizing for delivering door hangers it now says are part of a "known romance scam."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cyber incident disrupting services for Pacific Blue Cross members
candidates.description: B.C. health benefits provider Pacific Blue Cross says it's dealing with a "cyber incident" that has disrupted some of its systems, leaving members unable to access certain services, including its website and contact centre.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Niagara family business says $500K weekly in Trump tariffs is forcing production to U.S.
candidates.description: The company that manufactures packaging for ice cream brands Chapman’s, Baskin-Robbins and Van Leeuwen says it will shift production from its headquarters in West Lincoln, Ont., to the U.S. due to steep tariffs on Canadian-made exports.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Backpack reflectors: Alberta school pushes pre-dawn safety after time change ends
candidates.description: Elementary schools in Brooks, Alta., are handing out reflective tags for students to wear on backpacks as they walk to school or to the bus in much darker conditions this winter — the first after Alberta ended the practice of turning back clocks in the fall. Parents are welcoming the move.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CRTC orders Bell, Rogers, Telus to stop charging prohibited wireless fees by Dec. 27
candidates.description: Canada's telecommunications regulator says Bell, Rogers and Telus have charged consumers fees that are prohibited under the Telecommunications Act, and has ordered them to stop by Dec. 27.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Government reveals contractor shortlist for 24 Sussex overhaul
candidates.description: The federal government has made a shortlist of seven contractors it is considering to renovate 24 Sussex Drive into a habitable residence once again.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Jays tickets, drums and Tinder: Hundreds of purchases made with city credit cards raise questions about misuse
candidates.description: City of Toronto employees used city credit cards to make hundreds of purchases that included Blue Jays tickets, gift cards and later-disputed purchases on Tinder, an analysis of expenditure data by CBC News has found. The city says it has layers of oversight, but experts say it needs to be better.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kenneth Law apologizes in court to families of victims
candidates.description: Prosecutors are seeking a 25-year sentence for an Ontario man who sold potentially deadly substances online to people who then used those products to take their own lives.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This suspected North Korean operative said he had an IT company in Toronto. It wasn't real
candidates.description: For the last year, the fifth estate has investigated multiple suspected North Korean operatives posing online as Canadian residents. They have been able to secure remote jobs in Canadian companies and government, their paycheques propping up the heavily sanctioned regime.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This Independent is giving Poilievre's Conservatives the jitters ahead of a crucial byelection
candidates.description: The federal riding of Brantford-Brant South has been a Conservative stronghold for most of the last 20 years. But an insurgent Independent candidate who was passed over by leader Pierre Poilievre is trying to stop Tory rule in an upcoming byelection — and there are early signs he's gaining traction.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford says he wouldn't hesitate to shoot a home invader, encourages Ontarians to 'fight back'
candidates.description: Premier says he wants to see legal changes to address a spate of home invasions, and in the meantime is advising people to "use anything you can to protect your family."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. NDP MLAs sworn in, but David Eby absent
candidates.description: NDP MLAs took the oath of office in the B.C. Legislature on Thursday. Former premier David Eby did not attend the swearing in and will be sworn in separately.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman who stole $1.3M from Legion to 'feed her gambling habits' gets 6-year sentence
candidates.description: A Calgary judge has handed down a six-year sentence to a woman who stole more than $1.3 million from the Royal Canadian Legion to “feed her gambling habits.”
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cause of plane crash northeast of Toronto that killed teen undetermined: TSB report
candidates.description: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada released its report Thursday on the 2025 floatplane crash that killed a 16-year-old boy when the dock he was standing on was struck by the aircraft attempting to land.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta's Nakiska ski hill closure proves bears are still out
candidates.description: The Nakiska Ski Resort was temporarily closed after a bear was seen. Experts say many bears in the area are already in their dens, but it’s not unusual for some to stay out looking for food.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Zelenskyy criticizes Trump for cozying up to Putin as EU kicks Ukraine funding down the road
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized Donald Trump for cozying up to Russian President Vladimir Putin, delaying delivery of promised Patriot missiles and not paying enough attention to the Ukraine war in an interview with the BBC that aired just as an EU budget deal that was to approve a $70 billion loan to the war-ravaged country fell apart.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: War, fuel costs and aid cuts raise famine risk across 16 hotspots, UN agencies warn
candidates.description: United Nations' food agencies are warning that hunger is set to deepen across 16 countries over the next six months, as conflict, soaring fuel costs linked to the war in the Middle East and steep aid cuts threaten to push more people into crisis.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Breast bowl' from Marie-Antoinette's pleasure dairy sets new record at auction
candidates.description: A rare porcelain "breast bowl" — an unconventionally shaped drinking vessel that Louis XVI commissioned for Marie-Antoinette — has sold for a record-setting price at auction in Paris.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The corruption case against Benjamin Netanyahu just suffered a serious blow. What comes next?
candidates.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was handed a major legal victory this week when the judges in the years-long corruption trial against him suggested the prosecution reconsider one case, work out a plea deal in another and entirely drop the third. Here's a look at the cases, the charges, what the judges said and where it may go next.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Thanksgiving storm on U.S. East Coast knocks out power, disrupts flights
candidates.description: A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the U.S. East Coast on Thursday, knocking out power to nearly one million customers at one point as wind gusts of up to 112 km/h toppled trees and power lines.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Where big U.S. unions stand on Trump's Canada tariffs
candidates.description: While U.S. President Donald Trump insists his tariffs will bring a boom in factory jobs, the unions who represent hundreds of thousands of manufacturing workers are largely skeptical of his approach. Nowhere is that skepticism more apparent than big labour's view of Trump's tariffs on imports from Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A Boston man won $1M US in the lottery. Days later, ICE arrested him
candidates.description: Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales won $1 million US on a scratch ticket, the Massachusetts State Lottery announced Saturday. Three days later, he was arrested by immigration officials who said "his luck ran out."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iranian journalist, Oscar-nominated screenwriter Mehdi Mahmoudian arrested in Tehran
candidates.description: Rights groups are calling for the release of freelance journalist and Oscar-nominated screenwriter Mehdi Mahmoudian after Iranian authorities arrested him at his Tehran home on Wednesday, a day after he reported on an execution notice of two jailed protesters in Iran.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iran denies involvement after 2 Italian technicians killed in attack on Kuwait site
candidates.description: Two Italians were killed in a drone attack in Kuwait on Thursday that Italy and Kuwait blamed on Iran, although Tehran has denied any involvement.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Thousands march during International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women
candidates.description: Thousands of people marched at events worldwide on Wednesday to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. Here's a look at some of the best photos from the day.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Anita DeFrantz, whose trailblazing advocacy gave women an Olympic voice, dead at 74
candidates.description: Anita DeFrantz, the bronze-medal rower who became best known for breaking barriers to give women a long-lasting voice at the highest reaches of male-dominated Olympic policymaking, has died. She was 74.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nvidia scandal has put Singapore in U.S. sights. What's at stake for the city-state
candidates.description: The Nvidia crisis has put Singapore squarely in Washington’s sights amid concerns over its role in China’s access to advanced AI chips. Here’s what’s at stake for the Southeast Asian nation and why it’s stepping up efforts to prevent cloud computing companies like Megaspeed from circumventing U.S. export controls.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: FedEx airplane overruns runway at Miami airport, temporarily closing all but 1 runway
candidates.description: There were no reports of injuries after the plane ran off the runway at about 8:40 p.m. ET, the airport reported. By early Thursday, the Federal Aviation Administration was reporting hourslong flight delays.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ebola cases reach 12,000 in Congo as second-largest outbreak on record grows
candidates.description: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo now exceeds 12,000, government data showed on Thursday, as responders continue to struggle to bring the second-largest outbreak on record under control.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: FIFA says it has been victim of a cyberattack accessing 'personal and business information'
candidates.description: FIFA was the victim of a cyberattack that saw hackers gain access to what soccer’s world governing body describes as a “limited set of personal and business information," it said Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge blocks FCC review of Disney's ABC stations, says Trump administration appears retaliatory
candidates.description: A U.S. ‌judge on Wednesday barred the Federal Communications Commission from revoking Walt Disney's licences for its eight company-owned ABC TV stations, in a dramatic blow to President Donald Trump's efforts to rein in American media companies.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada Post narrows Q3 loss to $451M as parcel and flyer business picks up
candidates.description: The third-quarter loss is an improvement of nearly 17 per cent, compared with the $541-million loss in the same period last year. The postal carrier has been struggling as fewer people send letter mail.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Small businesses worry potential consumer pullback could cut into critical holiday sales
candidates.description: The holiday shopping season is a critical money-making time for lots of retailers. But as retail sales point to a dip in consumer spending, small business owners worry a pullback by shoppers could dent their sales.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A seasonal highway closure may be holding back tourism in Alberta’s Foothills
candidates.description: A section of Highway 40 is set to close for the winter on Dec. 1, leading some businesses in Alberta's Foothills to suggest keeping the roadway open year-round. But questions remain about the cost of winter maintenance and the potential impact on wildlife.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Data breaches are coming fast and furious. Are businesses doing enough to protect your data?
candidates.description: Recent data breaches at Bell and Staples are the latest in a swath of incidents where consumers' personal data was accessed by bad actors. As AI tools make it easier to carry out hacks, many businesses are trying to keep up with the onslaught of attacks — but security and data experts say poor data management and security practices often leave consumer information more vulnerable than it should be.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: So, your personal info was hacked in a breach. Here's how scammers use it against you
candidates.description: While it may come as a relief when a breached company says financial information wasn't accessed, that doesn't mean your bank accounts are safe.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford, Unifor call on Ottawa to exempt Canadian automakers from exhaust pollution penalties
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Unifor president Lana Payne are calling on Ottawa to exempt automakers from penalties for failing to comply with the government's tailpipe emission standards.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The threat of Starlink looms over Quebecor's Telus bid. But are Canadian telecoms actually vulnerable?
candidates.description: In Quebecor’s $31-billion bid to take over Telus, the theme of Canadian sovereignty is emerging front and centre as the Montreal company pitches a merger, in part, to battle the threat of American satellite companies like Elon Musk's SpaceX.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: China, U.S. allies push back on latest round of White House tariffs
candidates.description: China, Japan and other U.S. trading partners protested planned tariff hikes by Donald Trump's administration and hit back at allegations they have excess manufacturing capacity.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
candidates.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wants to defy the polls, and his main rivals accuse him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
candidates.description: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
candidates.description: Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Brazil pushes back on Macron calling its meat 'doped'
candidates.description: France's president made the comment while speaking to French farming representatives, months after the EU banned Brazil beef and poultry products.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law
candidates.description: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, will be sentenced at a later date.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed away from Ibiza
candidates.description: There are fears of a major oil spillage off Ibiza but the ship's fuel tanks are so far intact.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
candidates.description: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Italy's former police chief rejected mafia inquiry allegations before death
candidates.description: The contents of an eight-page letter by Gianni De Gennaro have been revealed days after his body was found at his Tuscany home.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
candidates.description: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing his followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands of people were without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
candidates.description: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Behind China's spectacular rise, voices who defied it say they are being drowned out
candidates.description: China's immense clout now also has the flex of soft power. Critics and dissidents say their voices are being drowned out.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Inside Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks test kingdom's image of security
candidates.description: Despite the strikes, markets and restaurants in Riyadh remain busy as residents express trust in the government to protect them.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly convicted over attack on UK couple
candidates.description: Evidence from a British police officer helped convict Ali Kololo over a 2011 attack in the Kenyan resort of Lamu.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
candidates.description: Female protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, a rights group says.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
candidates.description: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power a day after US slammed with Thanksgiving storms
candidates.description: Pennsylvania and neighbouring states remain badly affected on Friday after both coasts were lashed with wind and rain.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Floating nature islands installed in parks as Glasgow Games legacy
candidates.description: The islands, being planted in five Glasgow parks, are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Major Thanksgiving storm brings flooding, flight delays across US
candidates.description: Almost one million customers in the US had no power on Thursday evening as storms descended on both US coasts, bringing wind gusts, heavy rain and flooding.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Truck hangs in the balance after losing control in wet conditions
candidates.description: A semi-truck carrying mail was left straddling an off-ramp and an overpass in Toledo, Ohio on Thanksgiving Day during severe weather in the US.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Council to set London's highest littering fines
candidates.description: Fines for littering will rise from £500 to £750 in Harrow, while fly-tipping will see a £5,000 penalty.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
candidates.description: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: As UN Secretary General's last day approaches, search for his replacement continues
candidates.description: The UN Secretary General's term ends this year, but the big powers at the UN have been unable to agree on a replacement. UN watchers worry that there will be little time to get up to speed.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
candidates.description: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
candidates.description: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
candidates.description: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
candidates.description: The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Can luxury save Macy's?
candidates.description: This week's celebration of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving parade finds the department store at a turning point. After years of losing sales, the retailer is reimagining itself — as a higher-end destination.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
candidates.description: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 12 strategies to cut your risk of dementia. Take this quiz to start
candidates.description: Here's something you can do as you gather with family and friends this holiday season: Take a free, five-minute quiz to assess your brain health. You'll learn simple changes to keep your mind sharp.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Public health specialist discusses the aftermath of the munitions detonation in Iowa
candidates.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with public health specialist Will Sander of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign about the aftermath of the Iowa munitions detonation.
candidates.author: NPR
